'''Jean Marie François Joseph Coulomb'''<ref name=ras></ref> (7 November 1904&nbsp;– 26 February 1999) was a French [[geophysicist]] and [[mathematician]], and one of the early members of the [[Nicolas Bourbaki|Bourbaki group]] of mathematicians.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://annales.org/archives/cofrhigeo/coulomb.html|title=Biography of Jean Coulomb|last=Germain|first=Paul|publisher=COFRHIGEO|language=French|accessdate=21 April 2013}}</ref>

== Biography ==

Coulomb was born in [[Blida, Algeria]]. From April 1935 to 1937, he was a member of the Bourbaki group of mathematicians.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iecn.u-nancy.fr/~tenenb/PUBLIC/IECN_2003/IECN2003-031-042.pdf |title=Bourbaki à Nancy |last=Beaulieu |first=Liliane |publisher=Institut Élie Cartan |language=French |accessdate=21 April 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20050108214239/http://www.iecn.u-nancy.fr/~tenenb/PUBLIC/IECN_2003/IECN2003-031-042.pdf |archivedate= 8 January 2005 }}</ref>

He was a professor in the Faculty of Sciences of Paris from 1941 to 1972, and director of the [[Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris]] from 1941 to 1959.

He was director general of CNRS, the French [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|National Centre for Scientific Research]] from 1957 to 1962, president of [[CNES]] from 1962 to 1967, and president of the [[Bureau des Longitudes]] from 1967 to 1969.

Coulomb was the President of the [[Société astronomique de France|Société astronomique de France (SAF)]], the French astronomical society, from 1958 to 1960.<ref>[[Société astronomique de France|List of presidents of the Société astronomique de France]]</ref>

From 1967 to 1971, he was also president of the [[International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics]] (IUGG), and from 1972 to 1974 of the [[International Council for Science]] (ICSU).

In 1960, he was elected to the [[French Academy of Sciences]], and was its president from 1976 to 1977.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140805162402/http://astrogeo.oxfordjournals.org/content/40/4/4.38.full.pdf+html|title=Jean Coulomb 1904–1999}}</ref>

His work was in the fields of [[seismology]] (theory of surface waves), [[geomagnetism]], and [[meteorology]] (atmospheric electricity and the physics of clouds).

== Awards and distinctions ==
*1956 — [[Charles Lagrange Prize|Prix Charles Lagrange]]<ref>{{Cite book|title=Recognizing excellence in the mathematical sciences : an international compilation of awards, prizes, and recipients|date=1997|publisher=JAI Press|editor-last=Jaguszewski | editor-first=Janice M.|isbn=0762302356|location=Greenwich, Conn.|oclc=37513025}}</ref>
*1961 — [[Prix Jules Janssen]]
*1971 — [[Three Physicists Prize|Prix des Trois Physiciens]]
*1991 — Grand Cross of the [[Légion d'Honneur]]
*Grand Croix of the [[Ordre du Mérite]]
*Officer of the [[Ordre du Mérite Saharien]]
